title: Review: Sol fresh full review of PR #656 after repair 19.4.6.4
description: Fresh full read-only review of PR #656 after repair eshyra-o9bd.19.4.6.4 of review eshyra-o9bd.19.4.6.3 S1-S4. Exact head recorded at dispatch. VERDICT line at end.
notes:
Dispatched gpt-6.1-sol effort high at exact head 7d150a3c7fc47c58f1694fa815ce5d2210422a92; PGID 3470329
FRESH FULL REVIEW at exact head 7d150a3c7fc47c58f1694fa815ce5d2210422a92 (PR #656), profile rules-clause-complete + semantic-system. Authority read: AGENTS.md; design-and-pr-review-policy.md, especially From observation to finding / Findings discipline; importer-fix-protocol.md; ADR 0020; bd memories faithful; owning bead 19.4.6 including every note; children .1/.2; subsystem inventory 19.4.5.7 including identifier corrections; prior review .3 and repair .4. The user's faithful-or-absent decision governs; the unadopted per-ability contract proposal is NOT an approval condition.

Review scope: git diff origin/main...HEAD (origin/main e891b2eca8208acbe5296125b029214b3d5c01aa); 157 changed records, all magic items; no item description or mechanics.effects changed. Read-only generated-data enumeration and source comparison covered parent and variant non-effect structures across all 240 magic items: 362 operations, 49 machines / 126 states / 235 transitions, 149 economy pools, 30 grants in 17 containers, 10 containment blocks, 9 spellStore contracts, rollManipulation, interItem and randomProcedure/curse context. Read relevant printed tables and inherited conjure-elemental / item-spell authority. Reviewed table application, clause owner/tag selection, namespace and variant merging, withholding, compilation integrity, schema changes, tests, inventory and finding-registry boundary; reviewed the named runtime consumers, including discovery presentation.

Validation (repository files unchanged): six importer/schema/pack suites passed, 471 tests (magicItemOperationSourceAgreement, magicItemEffectSourceAgreement, alternativeOptionProjections, magicItemMechanicsSchema, magicItemLegacyCapabilityBacklog, srdGeneratedPack); six runtime/discovery suites passed, 135 tests (itemState, itemResetExecutor, usageCounters, magicItemVariants, projectionLimitProvenance, discoveryStages). Both runs used npx --no-install vitest run ... --no-cache --configLoader runner --maxWorkers 1. npm run verify:dnd5e-srd-pack regenerated only in scratch and passed exact pack plus five sibling-artifact comparisons. Inventory --check passed, 1926 rows. No format/full-worktree verification, repository edits, commits, pushes, GitHub comments or merge.

RUNTIME SAFETY: independently recomputed deriveItemOperationReadinessInput + assertMagicItemOperationReady on origin/main (1055 combinations), prior reviewed 767ab4f6 (1048), and this head (1049). Exactly the SAME 19 identities pass all three: Ammunition hit-target; Boots of Levitation cast-levitate; Candle burn; 14 Ioun Stone variant grab-orbiting-stone operations; Ring of Shooting Stars discharge-ball-lightning; Rope of Entanglement escape-rope. The consumers still ignore activation prose; operation/economy/effect references and via/timer ownership drive execution. Canonical items cannot bypass use_item through generic usage counters. The findings below concern existing emitted source claims and staged semantics; they do not allege these blocked operations have become executable.

PRIOR REVIEW DISPOSITION: .3 S3 (spellStore invented free costs) is repaired as a class in the current nine contracts; .3 S4 (necklace-wide per-bead pool) is repaired, with a verbatim adjudicated clause and preserved bead inventory. .3 S1 and S2 have repaired the named examples but are NOT closed as classes: additional conjunct loss and graph-state restrictions below survive. The original 19.4.5.7 non-effect members, including folded vcm3/Cube notes, were reconciled against emitted data; the remaining disagreements are batched below, including original S2.15/S2.21/S1.13 operation-side predicates and S4.01/S4.03/S4.06/S4.09 state-space siblings.

PROOF / DOCUMENTATION: verbatim sourceText is required by schema, its nonempty substring relation is enforced during compilation and over every adjudicated clause by the source-agreement tests. Patch application rejects missing operations, duplicate patches/clauses and source-span drift. These are sound lexical/source-identity checks, not semantic equivalence proofs. The whole-corpus operation census and all-machine graph-string census are complete for the fields they enumerate; item-level cost-word occurrence, the holding-word heuristic and verbatim graph strings do not establish conjunct preservation, topology or clock-anchor agreement. No generic natural-language theorem prover or new contract layer is required. Keep those limits explicit and extend proportionate class evidence for the concrete gaps below. Edited count/fingerprint, Orb requirement and sight-cohort expectations have source-backed explanations. The new Apparatus exact-edge assertion is itself too narrow (S2 below). Inventory is current; magic-item-effects registry truthfully excludes the present non-effect scope.
S1 — Activation predicates still lose printed conjuncts (the .3 S1 class survives repair). Invariant/authority: user's faithful-or-absent decision, memory magic-item-faithful-or-absent, owning bead 19.4.6, and each item's printed description; rules-clause-complete source -> selected projection boundary. A verbatim fragment is not an exact predicate when its governing conjunct is dropped; a nearby effect or a disclosed limitation does not make the separately typed activation exact.

Members / concrete distinguishing scenarios:
(a) Helm of Brilliance ignite-weapon, magicItemFaithfulOperations.ts:353 / records.json:104797: requirement only 'As long as the helm has at least one fire opal'. The property also sits under 'You gain the following benefits while wearing it' and selects 'one weapon you are holding'. An unworn helm with a fire opal satisfies the typed activation, and its operation supplies no held-weapon target. The repair notes disclose wearing as a 'known limit', but the user's decision does not authorize keeping a broader typed claim for that reason. All four spell casts correctly received wearing; this non-spell sibling did not.
(b) Hammer of Thunderbolts giant-slaying-critical, magicItemFaithfulOperations.ts:919 / records.json:103913: trigger types natural 20 with this weapon against a giant but still omits the Giant's Bane (Requires Attunement) header. The item has requiresAttunement:false for its ordinary +1 weapon benefit, so it cannot supply this gate globally. An unattuned wielder meets the activation fragment. The bound effect was repaired by #653, but this independently typed activation is still broader; hurl-thunderclap already carries 'While attuned to it'. The adjudicated critical-hit sourceText also starts after the header and does not carry the absent gate.
(c) Dimensional Shackles attach-shackles, magicItemFaithfulOperationsCorpus.ts:285 / records.json:98286, types target 'an incapacitated creature' but drops the printed Small-to-Large fit limit; an incapacitated Tiny or Huge target meets the typed target. Its designated-remove operation (records.json:98293) has only action cost and drops 'You and any creature you designate when you use the shackles': an undesignated remover meets that activation. The bound state note supplies size only descriptively, and there is no adjudicated activation span for these omissions. The repair addressed incapacitation alone.
(d) Ring of Shooting Stars move-ball-lightning, magicItemFaithfulOperations.ts:428 / records.json:122905: requirement types only the 120-foot maximum distance from you and drops 'move each sphere up to 30 feet'. A single bonus action moving a sphere 100 feet while staying within 120 feet meets the typed limit. There is no adjudicated movement clause preserving the missing displacement cap. This is original 19.4.5.7 S2.21, not a new whole-item ability.

Sibling analysis: checked all activation fields in parent/variant operations, containing predicates and the original non-effect inventory. Staff holding, elemental-ring plane/slay gates, Broom one-mile/familiarity, Iron Bands size/sight, talisman ground/sight/range, Mirror proximity and the green Rope/Ioun actor additions are repaired. The remaining members show header + local prerequisite, actor authorization, size class and two different distance roles; a holding-keyword-only cast screen cannot close them. Closure: make these selected predicates exact with the existing fields (verbatim governing spans where appropriate), or withhold the non-exact claim and carry the governing verbatim source span as adjudicated-by-design; do not keep a known broader field. Preserve the green set. Permanent evidence: generalized conjunct/recipient/geometry assertions with source-backed representative eligible/ineligible cases and an explicit sibling sweep; strengthen the existing screens' disclosures, not a new per-ability contract platform. Owner 19.4.6; material source repair; requires fresh review of repaired head.

S2 — Correct-looking graph strings conceal invented operation-state restrictions (the .3 S2 class survives repair). Invariant/authority: faithful-or-absent, owning 19.4.6, original 19.4.5.7 S4 stage/transition invariant, printed descriptions and Apparatus lever table. This is an emitted transition contract consumed by itemState, not a request to model every unrepresented ability. itemState.ts:1518-1537 finds every edge for an operation and rejects it from a state with no matching 'from'; missing self-loops/incorrect destination states therefore impose prerequisites. Current readiness blocks these machines, so the immediate consequence is unfaithful selected/staged data rather than a newly green runtime mutation.

Members / scenarios:
(a) Apparatus of the Crab, magicItemFaithfulLifecycles.ts:288-297 / records.json:88730: UP has only sealed -> open; DOWN only open -> sealed. Every lever returns neutral after use, and the source allows moving any lever up/down, including repeating UP with the hatch already open. The old repair's toggling error became rejection of repeated UP; DOWN while sealed is also rejected. The exact-edge assertions at magicItemOperationSourceAgreement.test.ts:874-883 currently require this narrower graph. Preserve the original source claim 'repeated UP does not close the hatch' with lawful state-neutral use, rather than excluding the use.
(b) Eversmoking Bottle, Lifecycles.ts:528-544 / records.json:100432: after closing, the bottle is closed but its cloud lingers for ten minutes; open-bottle has only closed -> cloud-open, not a source-eligible use from cloud-lingering. Reopening the closed bottle during those ten minutes is rejected although the printed activation has no wait-until-cloud-disperses gate. The growth timer repair is correct but bottle openness and cloud existence are still conflated in operation admission.
(c) Dancing Sword, Lifecycles.ts:346-367 / records.json:96759: grasping the hovering sword sends it to not-hovering, not held; not-hovering has no outgoing edge and launch-sword is allowed only from held. Grasp it after attack one and then toss it again with a bonus action: the source allows that new activation, but the typed graph has permanently disabled it. 'Move more than 30 feet away' and 'grasp it' are different physical results collapsed into one terminal state.
(d) Broom of Flying, Lifecycles.ts:457-481 and generated graph records.json:92914: send-broom is admitted only from parked. The printed remote command requires a familiar destination within a mile and travel alone, not prior landing. A broom still hovering after its rider dismounts in midair can be sent alone, but the graph has no route from its prior ridden state to that permitted command; landing is its only exit. The prior fix correctly removed dismount as the hovering cutoff, but retained the parked-only stage prerequisite.

Sibling analysis: reviewed all 49 graphs / 235 edges for state admission, repetition, outcome, direction, termination and reset implications. Outcome-controlled Sphere/Iron Bands/Rope edges are now source conditions; the two failed-check graphs with onFailure have an explicit outcome vocabulary and are not unconditional-hit siblings. Glamoured active -> active reapplication is a correct positive sibling. Rope of Climbing commands now share state-neutral self-loops, another correct sibling. Folding Boat no longer invents boat <-> ship; Immovable Rod and Pigments lifecycle wording is repaired. Closure: represent source-permitted identity/reuse paths and separate physical facts as required, or withhold a graph that cannot state them faithfully. Do not add unprinted events or defaults to save it. Permanent evidence: generalized operation-admission/reuse scenarios, including opposite direction in both hatch states and reuse after source termination; retain source-backed original count/termination regressions. Verbatim condition/note/termination tests alone cannot certify topology. Owner 19.4.6; material source repair; fresh review required.
S3 — Cooldown quantities keep the right number but the wrong event anchor. Invariant/authority: faithful-or-absent / owning 19.4.6 economy and lifecycle scope, 19.4.5.7 S6 quantity/gate-identity invariant, and the printed descriptions/tables. Source duration agreement requires event-role agreement, not just a matching number or unit. The default cooldown builder magicItemUseEconomies.ts:80-97 spends the pool on the initiating operation; itemState.ts:1757-1824 schedules availableAt from elapsedNow at that spend when remaining is zero. itemResetExecutor then restores the pool at that deadline. A grant note saying a different anchor does not rebind this operative economy.

Members:
(a) Ring of Djinni Summoning, UseEconomies.ts:531 / records.json:118678-118696: a 24-hour cooldown is spent by summon-djinni. Source: 'After the djinni departs, it can’t be summoned again for 24 hours'. Summon at t=0, concentrate for the full hour, departure t=1: source next summon t=25 hours; emitted economy restores t=24. EntityGrant's note correctly says departure starts the wait, but is disconnected from the spend/reset contract.
(b) Wings of Flying, UseEconomies.ts:661 / records.json:145180-145198: the 1d12-hour cooldown is spent by manifest-wings. Source: 'When they disappear, you can’t use them again for 1d12 hours'. Roll 1 and use the full one-hour flight: emitted deadline is t=1, exactly when the active timer expires, permitting immediate reuse; source deadline is t=2. Early disappearance varies the same missing anchor, so fixing one full-duration example is insufficient.
(c) Efreeti Bottle serving-efreeti.note, magicItemEntityGrants.ts:192: 'next two openings, each separated by 24 hours' substitutes opening-to-opening timing. The referenced table:efreeti-bottle row 11-90 instead has one hour's service, THEN return and a new stopper, THEN 'The stopper can’t be removed for 24 hours'. The next lawful opening is at least 25 hours after the previous one, not the note's 24-hour opening interval. Quote the actual stopper/return sequence instead of this different relation.

Sibling analysis: examined every hour/days/per-period/reset economy and grant cooldown text. Frost Brand's once-per-hour use, Horn of Valhalla's seven-day use cooldown, and Well of Many Worlds' opened-portal cooldown are initiation-anchored positive siblings; the traveling goat and study budgets use depletion/completion as required. Winged Boots' unused-period reset is a separate explicit predicate, preserved. These members demonstrate an initiation-vs-termination error, not a label-name complaint. The ring and wings operations remain engine-pending and are outside the unchanged green set; this is a source/staged-consumer defect, not evidence of newly enabled live execution.

Closure: bind these waits to the printed departure/disappearance/return event with a source-exact existing vocabulary, or withhold the misleading typed economy/spend and retain the complete verbatim lifecycle wait as adjudicated-by-design. Do not alter the source to retain the generic spend clock. Permanent evidence: generalized delayed-anchor scenarios varying full/early termination and nonzero elapsed use; source-backed positive initiation/depletion siblings and source table sequence. No separate test for every diagnostic mechanism. Owner 19.4.6; material repair; fresh review required.

S4 — Grant policy still drops control prerequisites or invents item-wide coexistence restrictions. Invariant/authority: faithful-or-absent / owning 19.4.6 entityGrant control/lifecycle/composition scope, printed descriptions, original 19.4.5.7 S5 control and S6 outstanding-instance distinction. Typed grant control and exclusivity must preserve the complete selected source permission, including when control starts and what entity is bounded.

Members:
(a) Pipes of the Sewers, magicItemFaithfulLifecycles.ts:715-725 / records.json:114932: the repair replaces the producer control text (which did include winning Charisma-vs-Wisdom) with three verbatim fragments, but drops 'If you win the contest' and the eligible-swarm clause ('isn’t under another creature’s control', within 30 feet while playing). Current control says uncontrolled otherwise; becomes friendly while playing; ends on a deaf start of turn. The emitted policy thus supplies no condition distinguishing a LOST contest or a swarm already controlled by another creature from a WON eligible contest. Continuous action playing alone is not authority to obtain friendliness/control. The start-turn hearing repair is correct but loses an independent governing predicate. No adjudicated grant clause carries the omitted contest; the only new pipes span concerns wind-instrument proficiency.
(b) Staff of the Python python-form.control, magicItemEntityGrants.ts:541 / records.json:136402: 'owner mentally commands within 60 feet while not incapacitated' drops printed 'On your turn'. A nearby, capable owner can issue a new mental command on another creature's turn under the typed permission. This mental command has no printed action cost from which a normal bonus-action-on-your-turn rule could supply the missing gate. Preserve the full source sentence instead of expanding the permission. No source-backed default-command finding is added.
(c) Iron Flask released-flask-creature.exclusiveInstance, magicItemEntityGrants.ts:409 / records.json's magic-item:iron-flask entityGrant: scope:item, recast:blocked invents an outstanding-released-creature gate. The printed capacity of ONE concerns a creature trapped IN the flask; releasing it empties the flask, and the released persistent actor remains friendly for an hour and then resumes normal disposition. Release A, capture B into the now empty flask and release B during A's hour: source allows both actors to coexist, while the typed grant blocks a second item-scoped release. This is a new sibling of original S6.05 Orb of Dragonkind (outstanding calls incorrectly blocked later calls), whose exclusivity this PR correctly removed.

Sibling analysis: read all 30 grants including lifecycle, control, count, exclusivity, cooldown and death fields. Elemental concentration exception, figurine creation/reversion source spans, obeyed-command steed reversion, individual Golden Lions, Manual eligibility/ashes and retributive bystander outcome repairs are retained. Bag of Tricks and Deck of Illusions correctly allow independent concurrent grants; physical transformed-staff/figurine or single-use-item exclusivity is a different source-backed boundary. Ring's same particular djinni is distinct from Iron Flask's replaceable captured occupants. None of these current grant consumers executes control or exclusiveInstance, which lowers current runtime consequence but does not waive the source requirement.

Closure: retain the complete conditional control sentence/paragraph with its actor, eligibility, contest and turn predicates; remove unprinted grant exclusivity or withhold any claim that cannot be represented exactly, with a governing verbatim adjudicated span. Do not put a contradicted policy in a typed field while relying on nearby prose to negate it. Permanent evidence: generalized control-acquisition/turn/coexistence cases (winner vs loser, eligible vs other-controlled swarm, owner vs other turn, occupied flask vs empty flask plus independently released actor); preserve the correct hearing/reversion source regressions. Owner 19.4.6; material source repair; fresh review required.

No requirement: the proposed per-ability contract layer, a universal semantic/omission checker, a complete item executor, or unrepresented subsidiary abilities.
No requirement: malformed-input/typo discovery permutations, arbitrary test-count targets, wording-only labels, or wholesale rewrites of unchanged discovery/capability architecture.
No requirement: a missing activation cost by itself where source-backed ordinary spell casting time already governs and no contrary typed cost is asserted.
No requirement: treating source-correct onFailure edges as unconditional success edges; the kernel explicitly selects the declared outcome.
No requirement: interpreting every typed-projection inventory disposition as source-semantic certification; its disclosed scope is field-level shape/bookkeeping.

Four blocking defect classes, all owned by 19.4.6. No findings are deferred as optional follow-ups. Current exact head and repository cleanliness confirmed before closing this review; parent bead is untouched.
VERDICT: CHANGES REQUESTED (4)
